chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Hammad from Hariz from Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the tithe on 'dhurah' (a type of grain), and he said: 'Dhzarah, lentils, salt, and grains are subject to the same ruling as wheat and barley; and whatever is measured by the sa' and reaches the awzan (thresholds) upon which zakat becomes obligatory, then zakat is obligatory upon it.'

key_terms.الذُّرَةُ: Dhzarah, a type of grain or pulse
key_terms.السُّلْتُ: Salt or a specific type of grain/legume
key_terms.الصَّاعُ: A traditional unit of volume measurement
key_terms.الْأَوْسَاقُ: The plural of wasq, referring to the threshold quantity for zakat obligation

ai.seo_question: What grains and legumes are subject to zakat and what are the measurement thresholds?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that zakat obligations extend beyond staple cereals to include legumes and salt, provided they are measured by volume (sa') and reach the nisab threshold of five awsaq. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle of 'illat (effective cause) based on measurability and storability, ensuring equitable distribution of alms across diverse agricultural produce.
